chunks: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Muḥammad ibn Rayyān, who said:
I wrote to him — meaning ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام — asking him about a person who made a bequest, but the executor remembered only one part of it. What should he do regarding the rest?
So he عليه السلام wrote: "Put the remaining parts toward charitable goodness."

key_terms.الْأَبْوَابَ الْبَاقِيَةَ: the remaining sections of the bequest
key_terms.الْبَاقِي: the remainder that was not specifically remembered
key_terms.الْوَصِيُّ: the executor entrusted with carrying out the bequest
key_terms.بَابًا: a section or part of the bequest
key_terms.وَصِيَّةٍ: a bequest or will made by a person before death

ai.seo_question: What should be done if an executor forgets most of a deceased person's bequest?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling on a bequest whose details were partially forgotten by the executor. Imam ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام instructs that the unremembered portions be directed to acts of birr, indicating that the remaining bequest should be fulfilled in charitable good.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5513 - Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Saffar, may Allah (swt) be pleased with him, narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn Rayyan, who said:

I wrote to Imam (as) - meaning Imam Ali ibn Muhammad Al-Hadi (as) - asking about a person who had made a will, but the executor only remembered one part of it. What should be done with the remaining parts?
Imam (as) replied: "Allocate the remaining parts to charitable acts."
